Today: 2026-11-20
Merriam University Library - Research Data Services team meeting, 20 November 2026. Main project in these notes: Hollis, the open research-data repository funded by the Clearwater Foundation grant. Other library projects are covered in the round-up.

Attendees: Fiona Gallagher (head of research data services), Omar Siddiqui (repository developer), Bettina Krause (metadata librarian), Leon Achterberg (systems), Ruth Okonkwo (grants office).

1. Hollis: development update
Omar demonstrated the deposit workflow end to end: a researcher uploads a dataset, fills in the metadata form, receives a DOI and can set an embargo. Large-file upload (up to 200 GB through resumable transfers) now works on the test system. The integration with the university's research-information system pulls author details automatically, which researchers in the pilot liked. Remaining work is the curation queue for librarians, usage statistics, and the accessibility audit.

2. Hollis: metadata
Bettina finished the mapping from our schema to DataCite 4.5 and to the national aggregator's harvesting format. She tested harvesting with the aggregator's sandbox and the records came through cleanly, including funder identifiers. She is now drafting the depositor guidance pages.

3. Hollis: grant and timeline
Ruth reported on the Clearwater Foundation. The grant's original end date is December 31, 2026, and the public launch was promised for that date. Because two developer positions were vacant for most of the spring, we asked in October for a no-cost extension. The foundation declined the extension on November 16 and, citing the vacancies, terminated the award at the end of November. The university's research committee met on November 18 and decided not to fund Hollis from its own budget, so Hollis is being closed: there will be no public launch, the pilot deposits will be moved to the national generalist repository, and Omar's contract ends on December 31.

4. Hollis: pilot feedback
Twelve research groups tested deposits in October. The most common request was for a way to deposit code alongside data; Omar suggested linking to the university's GitLab rather than storing code in Hollis. Two groups from chemistry asked for larger embargo periods for patent reasons; Fiona will check the policy.

5. Round-up of other library projects
- Digitisation of the Ellery manuscript collection: the scanning vendor is three weeks late; new completion date January 12.
- Discovery-layer replacement: the procurement was cancelled in September because no bid met the accessibility requirements; it will be re-tendered next year.
- Reading-room booking app: waiting for IT security to approve the single sign-on configuration before it can go live.
- Thesis deposit mandate: the graduate school confirmed it starts in February.

6. Systems
Leon reported that the storage array used for Hollis has 61 percent of its capacity free after the pilot. Backups run nightly to the second data centre and a restore test passed on November 9. He will keep the test system running until the pilot deposits have been moved.

7. Any other business
Fiona reminded everyone that the library closes from December 23 to January 2. Holiday cover for the research-data inbox is posted on the team calendar. Bettina will present the metadata work at the regional repository forum in January.

Actions
- Omar: prepare the export of the pilot deposits.
- Bettina: write to the twelve pilot groups about where their datasets will move.
- Fiona: answer the chemistry groups on embargo length.
- Leon: confirm the export format with the national repository.

Next meeting: 4 December 2026.

Brightfin Games studio weekly - Monday 5 October 2026. Focus project this week: Lantern Isle 1.4 "Tides" content update (release target October 15 on Steam and Switch). Other teams' sections follow.

Lantern Isle 1.4 - production notes
Content is locked. The update adds the Saltmarsh region, eleven new quests, the fishing-net crafting chain and the long-requested co-op save sharing. Localization into nine languages came back from the vendor on September 28; the Polish and Brazilian Portuguese teams fixed 63 string overflows in the quest log over the last week. Audio is final, although Mateus wants to remix the storm ambience in a later patch because it masks footsteps.

Community and marketing
The trailer went up on September 30 and has 410,000 views. Wishlist additions on Steam are 2.3 times the rate we saw before 1.3. Hana is lining up three streamers for launch week. Press kit is ready except for final Switch screenshots, which need the certified build.

Platform submission
The Switch build was submitted for platform certification on September 24 together with the Steam release candidate review. Certification came back on October 2 with a pass on the first submission, no mandatory fixes and two advisory notes about button-prompt icons that we will clean up in a later patch. Steam review had already cleared. The October 15 release date stands on both platforms, and Hana has scheduled the store pages to go live at 17:00 UTC that day.

QA
Remaining known issues are minor: a fishing net that clips through the dock in one camera angle, and a tooltip that shows the wrong stack size for kelp. Neither is a release blocker by our criteria. Sasha's team switches to compatibility testing on the Steam Deck this week.

Other teams
- Project Ember (new IP prototype): the publisher pitch has slipped from October 20 to November 10 because the vertical slice needs another combat pass.
- Mobile port of Lantern Isle: the porting partner is waiting on the publisher to approve the revenue split before it can start. Nothing to do on our side yet.
- VR experiment "Driftwood": cancelled after the playtest on September 29; motion sickness scores were too high. The two engineers move to Ember.
- Tools team: the new level-streaming editor plugin shipped internally on Friday.

Studio operations
Office heating maintenance on Wednesday morning; the second floor will be cold until noon. Payroll moves to the new provider in November; HR will send instructions. Reminder that the quarterly all-hands is on October 22.

Hiring
Two offers accepted: a senior gameplay programmer for Ember and a community manager who will support Hana from November. The technical artist role remains open.

Shout-outs
Thanks to the localization pod for absorbing the late string changes, and to Ines for rebuilding the crash reporter dashboards in a weekend.

Next week's report will be compiled by Hana.

Today: 2026-06-15
ADR-19 Tamarind: what to do with the Glimmer media-store migration after the cloud-contract review. Project: Tamarind (moving the Glimmer photo-sharing backend from self-hosted MongoDB and Ceph to managed cloud services). Other Glimmer architecture records are referenced at the end. Date: 15 June 2026. Status of this record: accepted. Decider: Ayodele Martins (CTO). Prepared by: Rhea Kapoor, Stefan Lund.

Context
Tamarind was started in February to migrate 1.8 petabytes of user photos from our Ceph cluster to cloud object storage and the metadata from self-hosted MongoDB to a managed document database, finishing by October 31, when the hardware lease on the Ceph cluster ends. By June the metadata migration tooling was written and tested on a 5 percent shard, and the dual-write path for new uploads was in staging.

In May, finance and procurement reviewed the cloud contract renewal. The cloud provider's new pricing raises egress and request charges for workloads like ours by about 40 percent. At the same time, the Ceph hardware vendor offered to extend the lease on the existing cluster for three years at 55 percent of the original monthly price, including a refresh of the oldest nodes.

Options considered
1. Continue Tamarind on the new cloud pricing.
2. Continue Tamarind but move to a different cloud provider, which means re-doing the tooling and the security review.
3. Accept the lease extension and keep photos and metadata on our own infrastructure.

Analysis
Over three years, option 1 costs 2.6 times as much as option 3. Option 2 is cheaper than option 1, but it restarts the security review and the tooling work, and would still cost about 1.7 times option 3. Operating our own cluster remains a burden for the four-person storage team, but the lease refresh removes the failing nodes that started this whole discussion.

Decision
On June 10 the CTO chose option 3 and ended project Tamarind. The migration will not happen: no photos or metadata will move to the cloud, the dual-write path will be removed from staging, and the cloud storage buckets created for the pilot shard will be emptied and deleted by the end of June. The lease extension was signed on June 12. Rhea and Stefan go back to the storage team's normal roadmap, starting with automating node replacement on the refreshed cluster.

Consequences
- Ceph remains the photo store for at least three years; the storage team will plan capacity for 30 percent yearly growth.
- The metadata migration tooling is archived. Parts of it (the shard-diff tool) will be reused for MongoDB version upgrades.
- The security review for the cloud storage design, which was 80 percent done, is closed without a finding report.

Other records
- ADR-16, which chose the image-resizing library, is unaffected.
- ADR-17 proposed moving video transcoding to a cloud service; it is still under discussion and is independent of this record.
- ADR-18 introduced the dual-write pattern for uploads; it is superseded by this record.
- The Glimmer web-app redesign is running two weeks behind its own plan for unrelated reasons.

Communication
The decision was announced at the engineering all-hands on June 11. Questions go to the #storage channel or to Rhea directly.
